societies.name: Blame! — human enclaves excluded from the City’s fabrication systems
societies.society: The film’s human Electro-Fisher enclave under autonomous machine-access rules

scope.period: The enclave’s continuing precarious life before evacuation
scope.population: Living human enclave residents dependent on access to the City’s infrastructure
exclusions: The final refuge’s unverified future economy
A single supplied ration cache as unlimited permanent entitlement

societies.description:
The City has functioning automatic production, including a factory that can make food rations and manufactured bodies. Its surviving human residents lack reliable access. Their problem is not simply failure to earn a wage: machine authentication and hostile enforcement determine whether the available productive system will serve them at all. This is a deliberately harsh automated-production comparison, with almost no guaranteed human floor. The temporary ration success does not solve the enclave’s continuing insecurity.

Effective control lies with machine systems that people can only briefly circumvent. The factory and its defenses need not be one perfectly unified intelligence for human control to be extremely weak. Survival still demands real expeditions, engineering, fighting and care; automatic productive capacity does not make those contributions vanish. A low nonworking estimate is therefore a broad interpretation of a subsistence-focused enclave, with room for dependents or residents unable to participate. It is not a canonical labor census. The later escape creates a different situation whose long-term distribution rules are not assigned these coordinates.

guarantees.basis: Food fabrication exists but access is fragile, authentication fails and lethal enforcement threatens users; no universal entitlement is established.

control.basis: Autonomous access/enforcement systems override human use, despite brief technical circumvention; no single unified AI ownership charter is assumed.

nonworking.basis: Subsistence, expeditions, maintenance and care suggest high useful participation; the broad noncanonical range allows dependents and incapacity without inventing an age census.

evidence.claim: Automatic factories can supply food, but human access is rejected and extermination machinery attacks.
evidence.locator: Film-specific automated factory and enclave food passages

uncertainties: An exclusionary automatic-production comparison, not a claim that humans enjoy freedom from survival work.
Genetic/access status and machine enforcement replace any reliable wage-to-goods bargain.
The numeric participation estimate is explicitly rough and source-dependent.
No manga-wide economic equivalence or permanent final-refuge policy is inferred.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

review_notes: Twelve short-check decisions and one explicitly exclusionary automated-production record.
Blame’s actual food factory is not just speculative machine capability; temporary access does not become a secure floor and human survival work is counted.
Appleseed biological Bioroids and cyborg workers remain persons doing useful work. Nihei organization names do not establish shared continuity.

A NOiSE URL returned 404; the readily available publisher synopsis resolved identity without reading the manga. Fan RPGs, crossovers, unrelated music and weak speculative station descriptions were not used.
